persona.who: 21, Indian-American senior at Rutgers, born in NJ. Parents from Gujarat. Dating a white classmate; hasn't told parents. Feels neither fully Indian nor American.
persona.note: my parents keep asking when I'll 'settle down with a nice Gujarati boy' and I've been with my boyfriend for 2 years and he's not Indian. I feel like whichever way I go I lose a part of me

understanding.bridge: The life they keep describing is not yours, and the choice they keep handing you is not the one that decides who you are.
understanding.core_struggle: An Indian student in a two-year relationship is being pressed by her parents to choose a Gujarati husband, and feels she will lose a part of herself either way.
understanding.mirror: Two years with the person you love, and the conversation is still about who is the right kind of boy.
understanding.insight: You are not choosing between a part of your parents and a part of yourself. You are being asked to shrink so they can feel at ease, and that is their work, not yours.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: My parents' expectations weigh on me. Being seen as less than you are by the people who ought to know you best, and the anger of watching the life you built get called a phase.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A woman of learning and standing, dismissed by her own family, who questioned them openly and stood in her truth until they had no answer.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on duties by nature and finding fulfilment in your own work.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम् ॥
verse.line: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, though imperfect, than the duty of another well performed. Doing the work born of one's own nature, one incurs no wrong.
verse.why: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.
verse.misuse: Not 'stick to the role you were born into'. It's about honest fit with your own nature, not caste or family script.

matched.label: My parents' expectations weigh on me

prasang.title: Duties by nature, and their fruit
prasang.summary: After listing duties by varna, Krishna says one reaches perfection through one's own work done as worship, and that one's own path, though imperfect, beats another's, since every undertaking has flaws.
prasang.lesson: Do the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on the battlefield, where Arjuna is frozen, unable to choose between his own nature and the expectations of those around him. Krishna tells him that it is better to follow the path that belongs to you, even if it is flawed, than to walk someone else's path perfectly. The truth is that every action has its rough edges, so you only create trouble for yourself by trying to be someone you are not.
verse.for_you: You are caught between your own life and the life your parents want for you, and neither choice feels like it leaves you whole. You do not have to choose their version of a perfect future to be good.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Right after naming the five causes of any action, Krishna warns about the person who ignores four of them.
verse.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
verse.line: If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
verse.translation: That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees himself alone as the doer does not truly see.
verse.why: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.
verse.misuse: Not a way to dodge responsibility; you are still one of the five causes.

prasang.title: What makes an action happen
prasang.summary: Every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Seeing oneself as the only doer is a mistake.
prasang.lesson: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Arjuna thinks he is the single cause of the war's outcome. Krishna says this is an untrained understanding. It is not that you are not involved. You are one cause among five. The mistake is thinking you alone made it happen or alone made it fail.
verse.for_you: Your parents see their own expectations as the only cause of your future. They act as if your choice is the only thing that matters. You are one cause among many. Your part is to know your own mind, not to carry the whole weight of their ease.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula speaks to her son Sanjaya, who lies defeated after losing his kingdom. She tells him not to hold himself in contempt and not to settle for little. She urges him to set his mind on what is truly good and to stop fearing. The point is that past defeat does not define a person. It is those who never try who never succeed.
verse.for_you: You feel caught and split because you are trying to hold two truths at once. The pressure to choose a Gujarati husband is not a defeat of who you are. You can set your mind on what is truly good for you and stop fearing the split.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः । शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
verse.line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
verse.translation: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung on you. By nature you are pure awareness; do not fall into smallness of mind.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: King Janaka sits before the young sage Ashtavakra. The king wants to know how a person becomes free. Ashtavakra tells him that the whole universe is strung on his awareness. You are not your body or your roles but the wide space that watches them. Freedom is not far away. It is already here, and it is bigger than any worry you carry. You do not need to earn it or shrink to fit into someone else's idea of you. You can let your mind rest in that wide space instead of falling into smallness.
verse.for_you: When your parents press you to choose a husband who fits their world, they are asking you to shrink. You do not have to. You can hold on to the truth that you are wider than this fight.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu speaks to his student Nidagha on how a free person moves through the world. Ribhu says to always do the work in front of you. Speak gently, read people's hearts, and let go of wanting or not wanting. Such a one neither grieves nor craves. They do not sink in the world because they are busy outside and calm inside. They treat the whole world as family and stay unhurried no matter what comes.
verse.for_you: do one small thing that keeps you whole. Call a friend who sees you, or sit with your books and let the noise from home fade for an hour. You do not have to sink into the pressure they place on you.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them.
verse.sanskrit: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उरःस्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verse.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.
verse.translation: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
verse.why: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

prasang.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
prasang.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
prasang.story_hook: Sugriva saw two archers walking towards his hill and was sure they had come to kill him.
prasang.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

verse.meaning: Ram speaks to Lakshman after Hanuman has just spoken. Ram notes how Hanuman’s words were not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained. They came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone. This is the way to speak when you want to be heard and trusted. It asks you to let your words come from a calm place, clear and steady, so they build trust instead of fear.
verse.for_you: When your parents press you, speak with the same even tone. Keep your words clear and not rushed. Let them land in the room like steady steps. You do not need to shout to be real.

story.title: Parvati holds to her choice
story.story_hook: The sages came to talk Parvati out of it, and they listed every flaw in the man she had chosen.
story.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
story.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

anchor.speaker: Parvati
anchor.setting: Parvati answers the sages who mock her resolve to win Shiva through years of austerity.
anchor.sanskrit: सत्य कहेहु गिरिभव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटै बरु देहा॥ कनकउ पुनि पषान तें होई। जारेहुँ सहजु न परिहर सोई ॥
anchor.line: Gold comes from stone, and even in fire it stays gold. Hold to what you are.
anchor.translation: You speak truly: this body was born of a mountain, so its resolve will not break, even if the body does. Gold too is born of stone, and even in fire it does not give up its nature.
anchor.why: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.
anchor.misuse: Steadiness is not stubbornness; keep checking that the goal is still worth it.

prasang.story_hook: The sages came to talk Parvati out of it, and they listed every flaw in the man she had chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

script: You are caught in the middle of your parents' plans and your own reality. You feel split into two people, and neither one feels like the real you.
Arjuna stands on a battlefield, paralyzed by the expectations of those around him, unable to move between the life he is being pushed into and the path his own nature demands. And Krishna replies:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वभावनियतं कर्म कुर्वन्नाप्नोति किल्बिषम्.
In plain words: Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.

Krishna says that your own path, walked imperfectly, is better than another's done perfectly. This is not about sticking to a role you were born into. It is about doing the work that fits you, flaws and all, as an offering. This is easier said than done, because the people you love are asking you to shrink, and that hurts.
You do not have to choose their version of a perfect future to be good. You are allowed to take up space in your own life without making them feel at ease.
Your own path is already yours. You do not need to earn it by being perfect.

depth.life: You are caught between your own life and the life your parents want for you. They want a Gujarati husband, and you feel you will lose a part of yourself either way. The choice they keep handing you is not the one that decides who you are.
depth.points: You are being asked to shrink so they can feel at ease. That is their work, not yours. Better your own path, imperfectly walked, than someone else's done perfectly.
depth.practice: Name one small thing you do that is truly yours, and do it today without asking anyone's permission.
depth.question: What is one small thing you do that is truly yours?
